analysis:
The PR changes only docs/operations/provider-release.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and a new rollback paragraph (head lines ~1033-1040, shown in the patch) describing `darkbloom update --rollback`. No source, workflow, key-handling or coordinator code is changed. The base unit (lines 886-1052) and head units (1-439, 440-885) are otherwise unchanged documentation of release steps, signing, cluster runtime facts and verification.

Security-relevant claim in the new text: the local rollback restores the previously kept release, quarantines the bad one, contacts no coordinator, and leaves auto-update on. This touches T-013/T-043 (replaceable binary, rollback authority) and the TB-003 operator boundary only descriptively. The rollback feature's implementation is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify: (1) that the restored predecessor is re-verified (hash, designated requirement, notarization) before activation; (2) that a revoked or unqualified build cannot be restored (T-054), given that no coordinator is contacted and App Attest runtime checks remain authoritative; (3) that the quarantine persists so auto-update does not reinstall the bad build. These are questions for the code-bearing change, not documentation regressions. The doc also cross-references ../provider/installation.md, which is not supplied.

The docs text keeps hash-pinned, no-overwrite semantics and permanent revocation as distinct from deactivation (head lines 1033-1037 region), consistent with the existing threat model. No new attack surface or invalidated assumption is identified from this documentation-only delta.
